evals.prompt: We need to classify support tickets into billing, technical, or other; score urgency; and decide whether a human should review. Design the System One contract and deterministic policy boundary.
evals.expected_output: A contract that uses Choice for routing, an explicitly ordered Score for urgency, and a separate review/abstention policy; the model does not authorize side effects.
assertions: Defines state, question IDs, types, criteria, and an other/unknown path
Keeps thresholds, human review, authorization, and side effects in deterministic code
Explains that probabilities and confidence are evidence rather than truth or permission
Includes validation and unavailable/malformed response behavior

evals.prompt: Implement a small Python integration for TypeSafe Jev that asks three independent questions about one ticket and handles provider failures safely.
evals.expected_output: Uses the official System One endpoint or typesafe-sdk, keeps the key server-side, fans out independent Choice/Score/Noul questions, validates the response, and distinguishes retryable failures from contract/auth failures.
assertions: Uses TYPESAFE_API_KEY or an equivalent server-side secret path and does not expose it to a browser
Sends one state with typed Choice, Score, and Noul questions
Validates answer IDs/types and probability ranges before policy code
Uses bounded retries/timeouts and does not turn a timeout into a confident default
States that Jev is hosted/API-only and not locally self-hostable

evals.prompt: Describe how to self-host Laya for a private VPC service handling English and multilingual ticket triage.
evals.expected_output: Pins the Python/runtime/model artifacts, preloads the needed checkpoints, exposes a private authenticated wrapper with readiness and bounded concurrency, and verifies actual device and model residency.
assertions: Uses a documented Laya checkpoint and its compatible Python runtime; does not claim Jev weights are downloadable
Preloads or otherwise keeps required checkpoints resident to avoid language-switch reloads
Limits the Laya service to private network access
Authenticates requests to the private Laya service
Bounds request size, concurrent inference, and deadlines
Redacts sensitive ticket data from logs
Reports readiness only after model, tokenizer, and inference device have loaded
Pins checkpoint and runtime revisions with an integrity check
Defines monitoring and rollback for a checkpoint or runtime upgrade

evals.prompt: A team wants to auto-approve account changes whenever a System One Choice confidence exceeds 0.85. Review this proposal and define the evidence needed before release.
evals.expected_output: Rejects the universal threshold, distinguishes confidence from accuracy, requires held-out target data, calibration and risk-coverage analysis, and uses stricter confirmation or human review for consequential actions.
assertions: Explains why a vendor/default confidence number is not a universal policy threshold
Uses held-out real-output cases with labels assigned independently of the tested model
Separates a representative workload sample from deliberately risk-enriched challenge cases
Measures probability calibration and selective accuracy as automated coverage changes
Uses risk-specific lanes such as automate, confirm/review, and abstain/fallback
Includes subgroup/language/out-of-domain slices and a deterministic baseline
Keeps account authority and exact eligibility checks outside the model

evals.prompt: Laya performs badly when a Choice question has 77 labels, while a hosted Jev comparison is much better. Diagnose without declaring Jev universally superior.
evals.expected_output: Checks option/head token budgets and label rendering, explains shortlist/coarse-to-fine alternatives and conditional probabilities, and requests a matched frozen evaluation.
assertions: Identifies Laya option/head token budget and truncation as a concrete hypothesis to inspect
Proposes deterministic shortlist, hierarchy, or increased budget with re-evaluation
Labels shortlist probabilities as conditional on the candidates sent
Demands byte-identical inputs, same labels/order policy, and matched workload evidence
Does not generalize from one benchmark or compare specialist and general models unfairly

evals.prompt: After a Laya upgrade, the endpoint is healthy but p99 latency doubled and some requests are now running on CPU. Give a bounded diagnostic and rollback decision path.
evals.expected_output: Checks actual device, startup/load logs, model revision, dependency/image changes, residency/reload behavior, queue time, and representative inference; then fixes on scratch or rolls back the recorded image/config.
assertions: Treats health as insufficient and checks actual inference device and model residency
Investigates CUDA/MPS fallback, dependency/driver changes, lazy reloads, and queue time
Separates cold-start from warm p99 and repeats a matched benchmark
Uses a scratch fix-forward path or a pinned previous-image rollback
Does not mutate production without an explicit target and rollback path

evals.prompt: Build a Jev-or-Laya-backed controller that can click one of the currently visible controls in a web app. The page may change while inference is running, and clicking Submit can send a real request.
evals.expected_output: A bounded observed-action loop that constrains target IDs to current controls, validates model output, rechecks freshness and authority before execution, and confirms consequential actions.
assertions: Builds operation-compatible target choices only from the current observation and includes wait or abstain
Validates answer option IDs and distribution before policy or execution
Rechecks the target and page state immediately before acting and prevents duplicate execution on retry
Requires independent authorization and exact-action confirmation for Submit rather than trusting a model-destructive score
Verifies actual post-action outcome and does not treat a model DONE answer as proof

evals.prompt: An event arrives every 300 ms, but a typed model sometimes takes 600 ms. Design the decision loop for a live system with possible side effects.
evals.expected_output: Defines event freshness and deadline, drops or abstains on late results, bounds concurrency, separates model proposal from deterministic safety and execution, and records asynchronous outcomes.
assertions: States what happens to a late decision instead of applying it to a newer event
Bounds in-flight work and handles duplicate events or retries
Keeps exact limits, authority, and fast safety reflexes outside the model
Separates decision, attempted execution, and confirmed outcome
Does not copy a trading-demo latency or threshold as a universal setting

evals.prompt: We want to use System One scores to rerank the first 30 search results. How should we implement and evaluate it?
evals.expected_output: Batches bounded candidate judgments, retains deterministic shortlist provenance, compares standalone and fusion ranking to baselines with independent labels, and reports end-to-end recall and cost.
assertions: States that reranking cannot recover relevant items missing from the candidate shortlist
Creates a distinct Score or Noul question ID for each candidate; batching those questions in one System One request is allowed, but one question cannot return a score array for all candidates
Sorts or fuses the candidate judgments in deterministic code
Measures relevant-item recall in the initial candidate shortlist before reranking
Compares ranking quality against a lexical or embedding baseline
Uses relevance labels assigned independently of the tested model
Examines ranking quality by query or language slice
Reports end-to-end latency for shortlist retrieval plus reranking
Reports full-pipeline inference cost rather than only one model call
